AdNJ3fydeao.summary: Svelte creator Rich Harris explains moving reactivity into the compiler and language rather than tracking state at runtime, with a history of spreadsheets as reactive systems and comparisons to React.
AdNJ3fydeao.why: The most recommended introduction to Svelte, credited with sparking its adoption.

AJdEqssNZ-U.summary: Vlambeer's Jan Willem Nijman shows how to make an action game feel great by stacking small effects like screenshake, recoil and particles onto a basic shooter. It was presented at INDIGO Classes 2013.
AJdEqssNZ-U.why: A perennial recommendation for anyone learning game feel and juice, praised for showing concrete steps that turn a bland prototype into a satisfying game.

AnrlSqtpOkw.summary: Alan Kay's tribute to Ted Nelson at the Intertwingled festival, presented using a revived Smalltalk-78 system running on emulated 1970s Xerox PARC hardware. It shows live, user-programmable software from that era.
AnrlSqtpOkw.why: HN returns to it again and again as a demonstration of how programmable and composable 1970s systems were compared with today's.

AvEqfg2sIH0.summary: The first episode of Stewart Brand's 1997 BBC series based on his book How Buildings Learn, covering how buildings change after they are built. Brand presents and the series has music by Brian Eno.
AvEqfg2sIH0.why: HN recommends it as a view of buildings as dynamic systems, with lessons for software architecture and long-term maintenance.

AF8d72mA41M.summary: Veritasium tells the story of how Shuji Nakamura and others made the blue LED, long thought nearly impossible. It covers the materials challenge of gallium nitride and the persistence it took.
AF8d72mA41M.why: HN recommends it as a gripping story of single-minded persistence against the herd, and as the back story behind modern LED lighting.

AxFzf6yIfcc.summary: Jonathan Blow's CreativeMornings talk arguing that business models shape game design, drawing an analogy between 1970s TV and HBO and between free-to-play and premium games. He calls for games that inspire awe rather than chase constraints.
AxFzf6yIfcc.why: HN cites it repeatedly in debates about in-app purchases and monetization corrupting games.

A8eCGOqgvH4.summary: Herb Sutter's deep C++ and Beyond 2012 talk on atomics and the C++ memory model, covering why programmers chasing top performance need to understand hardware ordering. This is part one of two.
A8eCGOqgvH4.why: HN treats it as the classic go-to for learning atomics and memory ordering, recommended over books.

A9UmdY0E8hU.summary: Sociologist and comedian Harald Eia argues in a TEDxOslo talk that Nordic social democracies produce more rich people per capita than the US or UK. He credits high taxes, welfare and strong unions for creating a safety net that enables risk taking.
A9UmdY0E8hU.why: HN uses it as a counterintuitive data point in debates on welfare states, social mobility and entrepreneurship.

AJ-auWfJTts.summary: A 2017 GDC postmortem in which Sid Meier and Bruce Shelley tell how Civilization came together from board game design and sim game experience. They cover its development history and design decisions, including fairness and luck.
AJ-auWfJTts.why: HN recommends it as a great account of how Civilization was made and as a source on perceived fairness in game design.

Agu6jipKfYw.summary: Evan Czaplicki's Strange Loop 2014 talk surveys the many formulations of functional reactive programming and how they relate historically and theoretically. It then shows how Elm's variant enables hot-swapping and its time-traveling debugger.
Agu6jipKfYw.why: HN people point to it as the clearest explanation of what FRP actually means and how its flavors differ.

APZCfmgzoS0.summary: A short explainer on the physiological differences between fasting and simply eating less. It covers ketosis, ghrelin and hunger waves, and the hormonal effects of fasting.
APZCfmgzoS0.why: Shared as an accessible, convincing case for intermittent fasting and its physiology.

AW3gaelBypY.summary: Wendover Productions examines why carbon offsets so often fail to reduce emissions, covering specific examples and the perverse incentives in offset schemes.
AW3gaelBypY.why: Recommended in greenwashing and offset threads as a well-sourced, detailed explanation of how offsets underdeliver.

AmgkSdhK4K8.summary: An older 3Blue1Brown video on why topology matters, built around the inscribed rectangle problem. It walks through how tori and Mobius strips appear in the solution. The channel later replaced it with an updated version.
AmgkSdhK4K8.why: Fans name it as a favorite 3Blue1Brown video, praising its detective-story treatment of the inscribed square and rectangle problem.

AyOAjFNPAbA.summary: James Hamilton's Tuesday Night Live keynote at AWS re:Invent 2016, touring AWS infrastructure at scale including networking, power and custom silicon. It also features NASA JPL's Tom Soderstrom.
AyOAjFNPAbA.why: HN treats Hamilton's annual talks as the best window into how AWS regions and hardware are actually built.

AD5aAd8Oy84.summary: Adam Savage and engineer Zach Radding examine Lumafield CT scans of Apple's $130 Thunderbolt 4 cable alongside cheaper USB-C cables. They explain the internal components that distinguish Thunderbolt from ordinary USB-C.
AD5aAd8Oy84.why: Linked whenever people ask why a Thunderbolt cable costs so much; the CT scans show the construction difference clearly.

Auuk1y4DRgk.summary: Michael Sugrue's lecture on Marcus Aurelius' Meditations and the Stoic ideal, covering the text and its philosophy. It is one of his humanities lectures known for their clarity.
Auuk1y4DRgk.why: HN recommends it as a classic, clear introduction to Aurelius, with some saying it helped through hard times.

AD4b-52jtos.summary: The introductory lecture of Richard Hamming's capstone course, The Art of Doing Science and Engineering: Learning to Learn. It focuses on style of thinking and on educating rather than training, using technical material only as illustration.
AD4b-52jtos.why: HN regularly recommends Hamming's lecture series as a fascinating, wisdom-rich course on how to approach hard technical problems and a career, often preferred to the book.

AbgsfeGvg3E.summary: Kevlin Henney's GOTO 2018 talk argues that much of what looks new in software is a recycling of concepts with long histories. It draws on history to show the slow, steady current beneath constant churn in frameworks and trends.
AbgsfeGvg3E.why: HN recommends it for historical perspective on software ideas and for dispelling myths such as the origins of waterfall.

Ak4on5uTaTg.summary: Patrick Boyle's deadpan account of Saudi Arabia's Neom and The Line megaproject, a planned 170 km linear city that has been scaled back to a fraction of its size. He covers the feasibility problems and the financing.
Ak4on5uTaTg.why: Recommended as the entertaining, skeptical overview of Neom whenever its progress comes up.

AGCmPLWZKd8.summary: David Kriesel's 36C3 talk, in an English translation, analyzes a year of scraped Deutsche Bahn data covering every stop of every long-distance train in Germany. It explores delays and how punctuality is actually measured.
AGCmPLWZKd8.why: HN brings it up in any thread about German or European rail as a data-driven, entertaining analysis of why trains are late.

ARYP83yNAWk.summary: Herb Sutter's CppCon 2019 talk on the split in the C++ community over exceptions and RTTI. He proposes making exceptions cheaper and more usable, including a zero-overhead, Result-like design.
ARYP83yNAWk.why: Pointed to whenever C++ exception overhead, bans on exceptions or error-handling alternatives come up.

AZR0UKxNPh8.summary: Kirk Sorensen's Google Tech Talk on liquid-fluoride thorium reactors, a design that could burn nuclear waste and use thorium as fuel. It draws on Oak Ridge National Laboratory work from the 1950s and 60s.
AZR0UKxNPh8.why: HN used it as the go-to introduction to LFTR and thorium reactor technology in energy threads.

Ac7G7xOG2Ag.summary: The earliest filmed version of the Turbo Encabulator technical-jargon parody, shot in the late 1970s with narrator Bud Haggert. It deadpans a stream of meaningless engineering language.
Ac7G7xOG2Ag.why: Used as the canonical reference for the jargon-parody trope, and as a joke whenever technobabble appears.

Av0PQDVTP4A.summary: Timothy Daly, an original author of the Axiom computer algebra system, talks about turning a large Common Lisp codebase into a literate program. He argues code should be written as readable manuals, and the talk was given at Write the Docs 2013.
Av0PQDVTP4A.why: HN recommends it in literate programming threads as a rare look at applying the idea to a huge, complex codebase, though some find it meandering.

AFVDZeg4RVY.summary: Ian Cutress interviews chip architect Jim Keller about his time at AMD, Intel and elsewhere, management advice, design approach, Moore's Law and x86 versus Arm.
AFVDZeg4RVY.why: HN recommends it as an interview dense with insight from Keller, worth hearing in full even for non-engineers.

AFnfTDbcPOA.summary: A long Team House podcast interview with James Lawler, a former CIA operations officer who led counterproliferation work against the A.Q. Khan nuclear network. He discusses HUMINT, WMD and how such operations were run.
AFnfTDbcPOA.why: HN recommends it as an in-depth look at the mechanics of intelligence work from a veteran who ran a nonproliferation operation.

AItTqnTsVjA.summary: Accursed Farms' hour-plus critique of the modern desktop GUI. It argues that current interfaces are a regression from older designs such as Windows 7 and proposes principles for better ones.
AItTqnTsVjA.why: Recommended as a thought-provoking critique that makes people notice how poor everyday GUIs are.

ALc8CBYOfkw.summary: Sabine Hossenfelder asks whether complex numbers are just a convenient tool or necessary in physics. She discusses a recent paper arguing that quantum mechanics cannot be done with real numbers alone.
ALc8CBYOfkw.why: HN recommends it as a short, accessible layperson explanation of the real-versus-complex quantum theory debate.

AZX6awZq5Z0.summary: Daniel Dennett gives a Royal Institution talk toward a unified theory of information, tying together evolution, learning and engineering. He argues that design can arise bottom-up through small steps without a designer.
AZX6awZq5Z0.why: Recommended for its account of competence without comprehension, relevant to evolution and to debates about AI.

AxCo2bE9Gtk.summary: Lawrence Lessig's 2011 Berkeley book talk based on Republic, Lost, arguing that money in politics creates institutional corruption in Congress. He calls it his favorite version of the talk.
AxCo2bE9Gtk.why: HN people point to it as a starting place for understanding how money corrupts American government.

AxZWxxZ2JGE.summary: Thomas Ricks's Nimitz Memorial Lecture at UC Berkeley asks why US generals did better in World War II than in Korea, Vietnam or Iraq and Afghanistan. A central point is the WWII practice of quickly reassigning or relieving underperforming generals.
AxZWxxZ2JGE.why: Used in hiring and management debates as an analysis of fast evaluation, quick dismissal without stigma, and the cost of keeping underperformers.

A0VYsiMtrNE.summary: A short music video by the Japanese group Electronicos Fantasticos, led by Ei Wada, playing festival-style music on repurposed old electronics. Instruments include CRT TVs, a barcode reader, an electric fan harp and TV taiko drums.
A0VYsiMtrNE.why: HN users share it as a delightful example of people making real music from obsolete electronics and self-built instruments.

ACkmg3Y64_s.summary: The official tour video of Miniatur Wunderland in Hamburg, the world's largest model railway. It shows the 1,300 square meter layout with trains, aircraft, cars and ships moving around.
ACkmg3Y64_s.why: HN recommends it as an absorbing look at the most elaborate model railroad ever built.

AIcfMMVcYZg.summary: Peter Schiff, during his 2010 Senate campaign, argues that government loan programs and subsidies push college tuition up.
AIcfMMVcYZg.why: Cited in tuition-cost threads for the argument that easy government-backed loans enable high prices.

AKGrmY8OSHM.summary: A roughly 10-minute guided Non-Sleep Deep Rest session voiced by neuroscientist Andrew Huberman. It is meant to reduce daytime fatigue, improve focus and aid sleep.
AKGrmY8OSHM.why: HN commenters recommend it as a short, practical guided rest session to use during a midday break or nap.

ASXJgvy3mEg.summary: Jared Mauch tells how he got fed up with poor internet options in rural Michigan and built his own fiber network to his town. The talk was given at NLNOG Live in September 2020.
ASXJgvy3mEg.why: HN points to it whenever community or DIY fiber ISPs come up, as a first-hand account of how an individual built one.

AZZNvT1vaJg.summary: Joe Rogan interviews Peter Boghossian and James Lindsay, who describe their hoax papers submitted to academic journals in grievance studies. The conversation runs about two hours and covers academic publishing, ideology and victimhood culture.
AZZNvT1vaJg.why: HN commenters recommend it as an entertaining account of how easily fake papers get published and of problems in academic peer review.

AdKNCBrkZQ4.summary: A short visualization from HotNets researchers of routing and latency over SpaceX's proposed Starlink constellation, based on its FCC filings. It shows orbital shells, link topology and how inter-satellite routes could beat terrestrial fiber on long distances.
AdKNCBrkZQ4.why: It is the go-to visual for how Starlink's constellation and laser links could cut global latency, linked in many satellite internet threads.

AdKUJxjn-R8.summary: BJ Fogg of Stanford's Persuasive Tech Lab argues that lasting change comes from tiny habits, such as flossing one tooth or doing one pushup, anchored to things you already do.
AdKUJxjn-R8.why: Recommended in habit and motivation threads for its simple anchor-then-tiny-action recipe.

Ag1AKIl_2GM.summary: Richard Stallman's TEDxGeneva 2014 talk describing how nonfree programs give companies control over users and what users can do to regain control. It introduces the free software movement and the four freedoms.
Ag1AKIl_2GM.why: HN uses it constantly as the reference for the argument that either the user controls the software or the software controls the user, and it is recommended as a basic introduction.

AnaASTBn_K4.summary: Smarter Every Day uses high-speed and Schlieren photography to show how a whip crack is a supersonic shockwave formed at the tip. It references academic papers on whip physics.
AnaASTBn_K4.why: Recommended as the clearest footage of a whip tip going supersonic, and cited in shockwave discussions.

Ao9iOeK_jvU.summary: First video in John Bartholomew's Chess Fundamentals series, focused on spotting undefended pieces. He teaches habits for scanning your own and your opponent's position to avoid hanging pieces.
Ao9iOeK_jvU.why: HN chess improvers recommend Bartholomew's beginner playlist as a clear, approachable path to getting better.

AwX9G38vdCE.summary: A long information session where The Boring Company presents its vision for Loop, an underground high-speed transit system, and the traffic problems it aims to solve. It includes discussion of faster tunnel boring and electrification.
AwX9G38vdCE.why: HN commenters point to it as the primary source for what the company is actually proposing, in threads skeptical of the project.

AxJubaijQbI.summary: Persi Diaconis explains on Numberphile the mathematics of card shuffling, including why seven riffle shuffles are needed to randomize a deck and how different shuffles compare.
AxJubaijQbI.why: HN points to it as a good, anecdote-filled introduction to the math of shuffling from the expert himself.

AyORieDhpkg.summary: A full-length album by The Kilimanjaro Darkjazz Ensemble, a dark, cinematic electronic jazz group. It runs about 55 minutes across nine tracks.
AyORieDhpkg.why: HN commenters suggest it as atmospheric, near-ambient music for programming and focus.

A9U5wK_boYM.summary: A reverse engineer walks through fixing a ten-year-old bug in Guitar Hero III without access to its source code, using a disassembler and decompiler. It is technical but explained step by step.
A9U5wK_boYM.why: Held up as a favorite tech talk and a great hard-debugging story about patching a game binary.

AGUwcs9qJXY.summary: Phil Vischer of VeggieTales and Holy Post gives an 18-minute history of racial injustice in America, covering why anger persists despite civil rights laws. It is told from an evangelical Christian perspective and adapted from a class he co-taught.
AGUwcs9qJXY.why: Recommended as a concise, broad-strokes history of racial injustice, including the lasting effects of redlining.

AJgY9FtDLbs.summary: Conan O'Brien interviews Jack White in a Serious Jibber-Jabber episode shot on 35mm film. They discuss White's creative process, his use of constraints and his approach to music and art.
AJgY9FtDLbs.why: HN recommends it as an inspiring interview about passion, minimalism and deliberately imposing restrictions on creative work.

AtPA6nIBs5g.summary: Captain Disillusion explains the visual effects behind the Back to the Future trilogy. He covers ILM's motion-control, computer-controlled camera work and clever pre-CGI tricks.
AtPA6nIBs5g.why: Recommended as a succinct documentary on motion control and practical-effects ingenuity.

A-fxij3zM7g.summary: Brian Douglas introduces Braitenberg vehicles, simple robots whose sensors are wired directly to motors yet show surprisingly lifelike behavior. He draws on Valentino Braitenberg's book Vehicles.
A-fxij3zM7g.why: Recommended as a short, fascinating introduction to how simple sensor-actuator machines can appear intelligent.

A0FZIwabctw.summary: SpaceX's recap of the Falcon Heavy debut launch, with side booster landings and a Tesla Roadster with Starman sent into orbit.
A0FZIwabctw.why: HN references it for launch footage and the atmosphere of the first Falcon Heavy flight, including the center core landing failure.

A2zKARkpDW4.summary: The official video for Boards of Canada's Dayvan Cowboy, built from reassembled documentary footage. It forms a dreamlike journey from space to the sea and shore, including Kittinger's 1960 high-altitude jump and surfing footage.
A2zKARkpDW4.why: HN mentions it as a favorite ambient track and as a nicely edited tribute to Kittinger's jump.

A3oIiH7BLmg.summary: An RSA Animate illustrating a lecture by psychologist Philip Zimbardo on how people's perspectives on time (past, present, future) shape work, health and well-being.
A3oIiH7BLmg.why: Recommended in threads about culture and time orientation as an accessible presentation of Zimbardo's framework.

A4UMyTnlaMY.summary: A short clip of Robert Sapolsky on how social hierarchy generates chronic stress, drawing on baboon research. It links rank-related stress to heart health and life expectancy.
A4UMyTnlaMY.why: HN shares it as a compact explanation of how hierarchy and stress affect health, pointing to the longer full lecture.

A5YyTHyaNpo.summary: Maker's Muse designs a 3D-printed and laser-cut puzzle box to test whether wild sulphur-crested cockatoos can solve it. He documents how the birds work it out.
A5YyTHyaNpo.why: Recommended in cockatoo threads as a fun and remarkable demonstration of the birds' problem-solving ability.

AHeZHyOnsm4.summary: Full recording of Elon Musk's January 2015 presentation and Q&A at the SpaceX Seattle office announcement. He lays out plans for a satellite constellation to provide low-latency global internet, tied to funding Mars ambitions. Pauses between questions have been edited out.
AHeZHyOnsm4.why: It is the primary source for the original Starlink concept, so commenters cite it for Musk's stated goals on latency, hops, pricing and timelines.

AHiNeUTgGkk.summary: A MIX08 session from Microsoft's Office team on how the Office 2007 ribbon was designed. It explains the user-feedback and telemetry behind it and the alternatives that were rejected.
AHiNeUTgGkk.why: HN recommends it for its in-depth view of a major UI redesign process driven by user data.

AI4ynXzkSQo.summary: James Hoffmann demonstrates his recommended technique for brewing coffee with a Hario V60 or other cone-shaped dripper, with notes on water and filter papers.
AI4ynXzkSQo.why: HN coffee fans recommend it as the reliable, simple recipe for much better pour-over coffee.

AUaJ8pDlxi8.summary: Louis Rossmann, a Macbook repair shop owner, goes through a long list of Apple hardware engineering failures, from GPU defects to keyboards and repair practices.
AUaJ8pDlxi8.why: Mostly cited by critics of Apple hardware quality, and as a rabbit hole for people curious about laptop repair.

AcQifPHcMLE.summary: Tom Scott visits the Swiss Military Museum to see the last surviving 1970s tank-driving simulator. It uses a real camera moving over a miniature model landscape rather than any computer graphics.
AcQifPHcMLE.why: Recommended as a great example of early VR and pre-computer simulation.

AcS3NOQnsQM.summary: A 1967 live film of Tom Lehrer performing his patter song "The Elements" in Copenhagen, reciting the chemical elements to a Gilbert and Sullivan tune. It is a short, polished example of his satirical piano-and-voice style.
AcS3NOQnsQM.why: HN commenters cite it as a favorite Lehrer song and invoke it as a joke whenever elements or science-themed wordplay come up.

AchISJUKfH4.summary: Megan McArdle's AEI Vision Talk 'Capital and Poverty' argues that social and financial capital work differently in low-income communities, and that this explains barriers to reaching the middle class.
AchISJUKfH4.why: Cited to explain why poor people's seemingly irrational financial decisions can rationally protect their social safety net.

AhRBsJYWR8Q.summary: A philosophy video critiquing the concept of human rights from a Marxist perspective, drawing on Locke, Marx, Nietzsche, Hegel and Rawls. It examines what human rights actually mean and presuppose.
AhRBsJYWR8Q.why: HN commenters recommend it as a deeper philosophical look at human rights from a critical Marxist angle.

Ai2HmvAXcU0.summary: A short video of a Boeing 777 wing being tested to destruction, finally breaking at 154 percent of its designed limit load. The wing is flexed upward until it fails.
Ai2HmvAXcU0.why: HN links it constantly as vivid evidence of how much margin aircraft structures have and that destructive testing is real.

AnZ0uTOerUI.summary: Michael Feathers' GOTO Chicago 2018 talk on reducing error checks and conditional logic in code. He offers a framework for handling errors and decisions at the level of code and architecture.
AnZ0uTOerUI.why: HN recommends it for the idea of giving data instead of asking for it, and ties it to zero values and exception-free design.

A-4dIImaodQ.summary: A Last Week Tonight episode segment in which John Oliver explains gerrymandering, how lawmakers reshape voting districts to shift political power. It uses humor and examples such as oddly shaped districts.
A-4dIImaodQ.why: HN cites it as an entertaining, fact-based explainer of gerrymandering tactics, though one commenter criticizes it as inconsistent.

AAsICMPwGPY.summary: Numberphile interviews Cliff Stoll about Klein bottles, the one-sided surfaces with no inside or outside. Stoll explains them with characteristic enthusiasm and shows off his collection.
AAsICMPwGPY.why: HN likes it for Cliff Stoll's infectious passion for topology, and it gets linked in threads about him and about Mobius strips.

AHs2Ugxo7-8.summary: A 2008 Google Tech Talk making the case for the liquid fluoride thorium reactor as an abundant, safe source of electrical power. It covers the technical motivations and design of thorium molten-salt reactors.
AHs2Ugxo7-8.why: HN people link it as the original, technically solid presentation on thorium reactors whenever the topic comes up.

AxnotgLql0k.summary: Andrei Alexandrescu's ACCU 2016 talk previews material from his book on writing fast code, with a focus on optimization techniques such as sentinels and faster search.
AxnotgLql0k.why: HN recommends it as a careful, entertaining talk on low-level optimization that shows how textbook algorithms can be sped up.

A1vyB-O5i6E.summary: A short clip of a frog levitating inside a roughly 10 tesla magnetic coil, demonstrating diamagnetism.
A1vyB-O5i6E.why: Cited as the canonical eye-catching demo of diamagnetic levitation, and sometimes used as a joke in magnet threads.

AE1gaNO9nj0.summary: Bjorn Nyland compares wireless and wired DC fast charging for an electric car, measuring end-to-end efficiency. The test shows the wireless system holding up well against a plug.
AE1gaNO9nj0.why: HN cites it as the evidence that inductive EV charging can match wired charging in efficiency.

AF2VyqSApjA.summary: A short demo of interactive AI live painting in Krita using the Stable Diffusion plugin, where canvas changes update the generated image immediately. It uses an LCM sampler for speed and needs a high-end GPU for the interactive feel.
AF2VyqSApjA.why: HN points to it as a demonstration of local, controllable AI painting and a way to learn the workflow.

AIZgw09CG9E.summary: A clip from the documentary American Tongues about the isolated Tangier Island, Virginia, whose dialect is among the most unusual in the US. It is often said to resemble speech from centuries ago.
AIZgw09CG9E.why: HN uses it as the standard audio example of the Tangier accent in discussions of archaic or colonial-era English.

AIxY_Y9TGWI.summary: Composer Tantacrul explores how corporatism produces soulless background music, and how some companies use such music in propaganda-style campaigns. He composes several corporate styles to show their tropes, with some music theory along the way.
AIxY_Y9TGWI.why: HN uses it as a go-to critique of bland corporate music and as a punchline whenever a slick corporate video appears.

AJ2keSJzYyY.summary: John Oliver's Last Week Tonight segment on freight trains and railroads, covering how profit-driven practices undermine safety. It touches on longer trains and shrinking crews.
AJ2keSJzYyY.why: Cited as a solid overview of the railroad safety problem, including the push toward longer trains and single-person crews.

ALaTm6VzTBw.summary: CGP Grey argues that the two-day weekend is poorly structured and proposes taking days off midweek, such as Wednesday and Sunday, instead.
ALaTm6VzTBw.why: Brought up in four-day-week and work-schedule threads as the 'Weekend Wednesday' idea.

ARKbfWk4Xyw.summary: Raymond Hettinger's PyBay 2018 keynote on preventing, finding and fixing bugs under a time budget. He covers testing practice, type annotation tradeoffs and the limits of coverage metrics.
ARKbfWk4Xyw.why: HN cites it in Python testing and code quality threads, including his point that 100% coverage proves little.

AXlyMrv8_dQ.summary: A short romantic comedy by Ted Nelson about the 'microcircuitry of love', with Doug Engelbart as his father and Stewart Brand as the villainous CEO.
AXlyMrv8_dQ.why: Mentioned in Nelson and Engelbart threads as a curiosity with amusing cameos by computing pioneers.

AYshVbcEmUc.summary: A short Apple promotional video about Liam, a robot that disassembles old iPhones so their materials can be recovered. It frames the robot as part of Apple's product life cycle and recycling story.
AYshVbcEmUc.why: Cited in repair and recycling threads as Apple's showcase of its iPhone disassembly robot, and sometimes mocked as marketing for what is really shredding.

AaTRHFaaPG8.summary: A three-hour Lex Fridman podcast conversation with AI researcher Eliezer Yudkowsky about the dangers of superintelligent AI and his argument that it could end human civilization. It covers AI alignment, why he thinks LLM capabilities are poorly understood, and the case for extreme caution.
AaTRHFaaPG8.why: Mostly cited as the canonical statement of AI doomer views, with some recommending it and many criticizing it as irresponsible or wrong.

AaZ_RSt0KP8.summary: Veritasium explains how cosmic rays and other particles flip bits in computer memory, with examples including a Belgian election count error, plane incidents and game glitches. It is inspired by a RadioLab episode on bit flips.
AaZ_RSt0KP8.why: Commenters link it whenever bit flips, cosmic ray errors or unexplained computer glitches come up, as a good accessible explanation.

AbSehcT19u0.summary: A short scene from Malcolm in the Middle in which Hal tries to fix a light bulb and is pulled into a growing chain of side repairs.
AbSehcT19u0.why: The standard illustration of yak shaving, dependency hell and getting derailed, also likened to adult ADHD.

Ae9EKCyI1xU.summary: Tom 7 (suckerpinch) delivers a long, comedic digression on gradient descent and floating-point imprecision. He shows how rounding behavior can supply the nonlinearity needed to build a neural network.
Ae9EKCyI1xU.why: Cited as a fun, unconventional example of neural networks built from floating point error.

AfKZclMWS1U.summary: A colorized clip from the 1970 Polish comedy film 'How I Unleashed World War II' in which a character must pronounce the tongue-twisting name Grzegorz Brzeczyszczykiewicz for a Gestapo officer.
AfKZclMWS1U.why: Mostly posted as a joke in threads about Polish, Unicode or hard-to-pronounce names, and loved as a comedy scene.

AgkfIQ4IGaM.summary: A short demo of the Deep Visualization Toolbox, which shows the activations inside a convolutional neural network as it processes live camera input. Viewers see individual units responding to edges, faces and text.
AgkfIQ4IGaM.why: HN points to it as an intuitive way to see what hidden layers of a convnet learn, and as a reference for hierarchical feature learning.

AjSl4n_KdOY.summary: A short FoundMyFitness explainer on the trade-off between growth hormone/IGF-1 and longevity. Higher IGF-1 helps muscle and cognition, while lower levels are linked to longer lifespan and stress resistance.
AjSl4n_KdOY.why: Linked in discussions of diet, aging and cancer as a quick summary of how IGF-1 and mTOR growth signaling cut against longevity.

AouW9_jyZck.summary: Engineering Explained examines BMW's Hydrogen 7, a V12 that burns liquid hydrogen or gasoline. He covers cryogenic storage at -253C and why the approach is impractical.
AouW9_jyZck.why: Cited in hydrogen threads as a clear explanation of why burning hydrogen in engines is a poor idea.

AqDdWEiSwMM.summary: Andrew Kelley's roadmap talk on upcoming Zig compiler milestones, focused on compilation speed. It was given at a Zig community event in 2022.
AqDdWEiSwMM.why: Shared as the place to see where the Zig project is heading, especially on compiler performance.

AqeJzItldSQ.summary: Footage of an unmanned Apollo boilerplate capsule launched on a Little Joe II booster to test the launch escape system. The booster went out of control and broke up, but the escape system worked and the capsule was recovered undamaged.
AqeJzItldSQ.why: HN cites it as the classic example of a launch abort test that proved the design even though the rocket failed.

AtK_YsVInw8.summary: A clip of George Carlin riffing on advertising and the nonsense around it, taken from a longer piece tied to the Zeitgeist movie.
AtK_YsVInw8.why: Brought up as a comic touchstone in discussions of advertising, usually with a joke or a quick reference.

A3AdN7U24iU.summary: Carol Nichols' Philly ETE 2019 talk on what makes Rust unique. It covers memory safety, how editions let the language evolve without breaking code, and who relies on Rust in production.
